articles.title: TSA program will allow some people to go through security without a ticket
articles.summary: The Transportation Security Administration has launched a new program at 13 airports, allowing eligible TSA PreCheck members without plane tickets to pass th...
articles.body:
For decades, the airport security checkpoint has marked the end of the road for friends and relatives seeing off a traveler. That is changing for some travelers.

The Transportation Security Administration has launched a new program at some U.S. airports allowing eligible TSA PreCheck members without plane tickets to pass through security and enter the gates, reviving a tradition that largely disappeared after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks nearly 25 years ago.

"As an exclusive benefit for our most trusted travelers, this new program makes it easier to return to the gate for welcomes and send-offs, meet friends during a layover, and enjoy dining and shopping along the way, bringing back the moments that once defined air travel," TSA said on its website.

Before 9/11, people without tickets generally could accompany travelers to the gate. The attacks prompted sweeping changes to airport security, including restrictions on access to secure areas of airports.

The program, called "Gateside by TSA PreCheck," is free, but people must apply online one to three days before their planned visit and receive approval before going to the airport. If approved, they can enter through a TSA PreCheck lane with an acceptable form of identification. The pass is valid for one calendar day, and visitors can re-enter that day.

TSA says members of other trusted-traveler programs who have a Known Traveler Number also can apply for access to the gates.

The program is initially available at 13 airports, including Los Angeles International Airport, Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas and Salt Lake City International Airport, according to TSA. But the agency says it plans to expand the program to more airports in the coming months.

Several airports throughout the country already have their own version of the program. Pittsburgh International Airport launched the myPITpass in 2017, although the program was suspended during the COVID-19 pandemic and remained on hold during construction at the airport.

Seattle-Tacoma International Airport began a similar program a year later, allowing gate access for up to 300 people without tickets a day. Other airports that have their own versions of the program include Philadelphia International Airport and Kansas City International Airport.

articles.title: Irã diz ter atacado 10 embarcações no Golfo Pérsico após EUA afundarem petroleiros iranianos | G1
articles.standfirst: Guarda Revolucionária diz que dois navios dos EUA e outros oito petroleiros foram afetados.
articles.summary: Guarda Revolucionária diz que dois navios dos EUA e outros oito petroleiros foram afetados.
articles.body:
A Guarda Revolucionária do Irã afirmou ter atacado dois navios americanos e oito petroleiros no Golfo Pérsico nesta quarta-feira (9). Segundo o comunicado divulgado pelo grupo, a ofensiva é uma resposta ao que chamou de ataque dos EUA a cinco petroleiros iranianos.

O grupo afirmou ter atacado 10 navios que tentavam atravessar o que descreveu como uma área "proibida e insegura" do Estreito de Ormuz.

Horas antes, o Comando Central das Forças Armadas dos Estados Unidos divulgou imagens dos navios petroleiros iranianos destruídos em ataques americanos afundando no Golfo de Omã.

O navio-tanque M/T Riesco foi atingido por forças do Comando Central dos EUA (Centcom). Segundo os norte-americanos, a embarcação estava sendo usada pela Guarda Revolucionária do Irã em uma rede clandestina de transporte de petróleo.

As imagens divulgadas pelos EUA mostram o momento do ataque. Na sequência, a embarcação aparece inclinada e parcialmente submersa. Em outro vídeo, é possível ver o navio pegando fogo.

Quatro dos petroleiros iranianos, incluindo o Riesco, estavam no Golfo de Omã. O quinto, identificado como M/T Derya, foi atingido nas proximidades da ilha de Kharg.

Antes de destruir os petroleiros, as forças americanas disseram ter ordenado que as tripulações abandonassem as embarcações.

Os Estados Unidos afirmam que os ataques foram uma resposta a duas tentativas fracassadas da Guarda Revolucionária de atingir um navio de guerra americano com mísseis balísticos nos últimos dois dias.

O secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio, afirmou que os Estados Unidos continuarão atacando petroleiros iranianos caso a Guarda Revolucionária tente atingir embarcações militares americanas.

"O Irã continua tentando atacar navios da Marinha dos EUA e, sempre que o fizer ou tentar fazê-lo, perderá navios-tanque. Acredito que vocês verão isso acontecer novamente hoje", disse ele a jornalistas durante uma visita à Colômbia.

Já o Irã afirmou ter retaliado o bombardeio com ataques contra a base americana de Al Azraq, na Jordânia, e dois destróieres dos Estados Unidos. O governo jordaniano disse que os mísseis iranianos foram abatidos.

A Associação de Pais e Amigos dos Excepcionais (APAE) é uma organização sem fins lucrativos que promove a atenção integral a pessoas com deficiência intelectual e múltipla. Presente em Montes Claros desde 1970, a instituição tem sua sede no bairro Jaraguá e atende mensalmente cerca de mil pessoas.

A gerente administrativa Maria Cleune Gomes conta que os atendimentos da APAE se dividem em atendimentos de saúde, como reabilitação intelectual e visual; atendimentos em educação, incluindo Escola Especial, Educação Infantil, Fundamental I e Educação de Jovens e Adultos; assistência social, voltada aos familiares dos atendidos, além de um Centro Dia; e diversos outros projetos, realizados através de parcerias.

Desta forma, ciente da importância do trabalho realizado pela APAE, o Município de Montes Claros está doando um veículo 0 km, tipo van, com capacidade de 9 passageiros, para ser utilizado pela instituição e que melhorará as condições de transporte dos atendidos, assegurando deslocamento seguro, acessível e adequado para consultas, tratamentos, terapias, atividades educacionais e demais serviços essenciais, contribuindo diretamente para a promoção da dignidade, autonomia e inclusão social.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police Tuesday apprehended the labour contractor who was supervising ongoing construction at Satya Niketan student hostel which collapsed Sunday, killing seven people. Sanoj was apprehended from Kasganj, UP, and was brought to Delhi.The FIR registered in the case states that building owner Hariram Gupta and his brother, to earn more rental income, constructed four additional floors on top of the old structure despite being aware that the foundation was not capable of bearing the weight.During interrogation, Mahesh Gupta, who was managing the accommodation on behalf of his parents Hariram and Urmila, said the building was given to PG operator ‘Hostel Daze’ on lease in Aug 2025. Two shops on the ground floor were being merged and expanded into one, police confirmed.Sources said a load-bearing wall was allegedly removed during the construction, which may have compromised the stability of the building, eventually leading to the collapse. “Mahesh was questioned about the construction and documents related to its possession and ownership,” a police source said.Police sources also said soil samples from the site were collected for forensic examination to determine whether the soil or foundation showed signs of disturbance, excavation, water seepage or weakening.Unaware of legalities in PG agreement, says ownerGupta has claimed that the basement was being repaired as water was getting accumulated during rains for the past 8-10 days. They found out about the building collapse from locals and fled to Gupta’s in-laws’ house in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan,” a senior police officer said.A court has sent Hariram and Urmila to 14 days’ judicial custody, while Gupta is on police remand for two days.Gupta has also been confronted with an alleged rent agreement draft that surfaced Monday and seemed to be aimed at absolving the owners in case of a mishap. articles.title: 'Suffered from hypertension, diabetes': Ex-Delhi chief secretary dies by suicide; note says no one responsible
articles.summary: NOIDA: Former Delhi chief secretary and municipal commissioner Rakesh Mehta, 74, was found dead at his rented flat in Sector 82 on Sunday afternoon.Po.
articles.body: NOIDA: Former Delhi chief secretary and municipal commissioner Rakesh Mehta, 74, was found dead at his rented flat in Sector 82 on Sunday afternoon.Police recovered a one-page note in which the retired bureaucrat referred to his illnesses and stated that no one was responsible for his death.Mehta had been living alone at Central Vihar-2 for around five years. His wife, also a retired Delhi-cadre IAS officer, and their son live in Dehradun, while their married daughter is based in London. Family members visited him in Noida from time to time.According to police, Mehta's wife last spoke to him on Saturday night. When repeated calls went unanswered on Sunday afternoon, family members alerted the society's security staff. Two guards went to his flat and found him dead in one of the rooms. A police team and a relative living nearby arrived soon afterwards.A forensic team examined the flat and collected evidence before the body was sent for an autopsy. Till late Tuesday night, the family had not lodged any complaint, though police said an inquiry had been initiated into the circumstances surrounding the death.Family members said Mehta had been suffering from hypertension, diabetes and other health problems, including tremors in his right hand and leg.A 1975-batch AGMUT-cadre IAS officer, Mehta took charge as Delhi chief secretary in December 2007 during the Sheila Dikshit government's tenure and remained in the post until 2010. His tenure included preparations for the 2010 Commonwealth Games, one of the biggest administrative challenges faced by the capital.Before becoming chief secretary, Mehta served in several key positions, including as MCD commissioner, chairman and managing director of Delhi Transport Corporation, and secretary (power). He was known for his focus on urban governance and public transport.During his stint at DTC, Mehta oversaw the transition away from the accident-prone Blue Line buses and the introduction of low-floor buses, which went on to become a familiar feature of Delhi's roads.Known as a media-savvy bureaucrat who pushed new projects and reforms, Mehta unveiled a 10-point agenda after taking charge as chief secretary. He also advocated greater transparency in civic administration, including changes to building bylaws, and promoted the use of technology to bring government services closer to citizens.Mehta studied at St Stephen's College, JNU and the London School of Economics. The caption accompanying the video identifies the location as the Muwaffaq Salti Airbase in Jordan.The strike came as Iran and the United States resumed exchanging fire in recent days following a month of relative calm in August. articles.title: A woman fleeing the Palisades Fire got her car stuck on a boulder as flames closed in; the same boulder may have stopped her from driving into the fire
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A year after the Palisades Fire turned a desperate escape from Malibu into a fight for survival, Patty Phillips returned to the place where she nearly.
articles.body: A year after the Palisades Fire turned a desperate escape from Malibu into a fight for survival, Patty Phillips returned to the place where she nearly lost her life. In January 2025, Phillips was trying to evacuate with her dog, Koda, when her car became stuck on a boulder along a dirt road near Big Rock Drive. Flames were closing in, while thick smoke made it difficult for Phillips to see outside. Fearing she might not survive, she waited for help as her husband, James, searched for someone willing to reach her. As per CBS News, he eventually found Los Angeles County Fire Captain Malcolm Dicks, who agreed to enter the fire zone with him.They found Phillips by following the sound of her car horn and spotting its lights through the smoke. Dicks then helped bring Phillips and her dog, Koda, to safety. A year later, the two reunited at the same spot where the rescue was done. The large rock that had trapped Phillips’ car was still there but was moved outside, serving as a lasting reminder of the moment that nearly ended in tragedy but ultimately helped lead her to safety.How Patty Phillips became trapped in Malibu during the Palisades FirePatty Phillips was trying to escape her Malibu home on January 7, 2025, as the Palisades Fire spread around her. She accidentally drove onto a dirt road near Big Rock Drive where rocks blocked the way. When she tried to reverse, her car became stuck on a boulder. Smoke and flames surrounded the area, which left her unable to see the road or find another route. Her husband, James, had already reached the Pacific Coast Highway and was looking for someone who could reach her. After several firefighters declined, he found Captain Malcolm Dicks. Dicks agreed to go with him and drove into the fire zone to search for Phillips.How Captain Malcolm Dicks found Phillips inside the fire zoneDicks and James eventually found Phillips by listening to her car horn and spotting its lights through the smoke. Phillips was trapped inside with Koda, her dog, while flames burned across the hillsides. Dicks reached the car and helped move Phillips and Koda away from danger. The rescue brought everyone out safely. Phillips described Dicks as a brave man who had risked his life when others could not come. She had sent messages to her husband while trapped, including one saying she was in big trouble. Another message stopped abruptly after she wrote that her car would not move and the fire was nearby. Phillips came to believe that the boulder had played a crucial role in saving her life.Why Phillips returned to the rescue site one year laterA year after the rescue, Phillips and Dicks returned to the area near Big Rock Drive to remember what happened. The reunion gave Phillips a chance to thank the firefighter who had entered the fire zone to find her. She wanted Dicks to see the boulder that had stopped her car and, in her view, prevented a more dangerous fall into the fire. Phillips had already reunited with Dicks weeks after the rescue, but the later meeting was also important. The location allowed them to revisit the moment when smoke filled the sky, and flames covered the hills. It also brought together Phillips, her husband James, and Dicks at the place where their lives became connected by the rescue.How the boulder became a lasting reminder of Phillips' survivalThe boulder that trapped Phillips’ car now remains outside her home with a plaque marking the moment that she believes it helped save her life. The inscription remembers Dicks, her husband James, Koda(dog), and a cat (Socks). Dicks was honoured by Los Angeles County leaders for his bravery during the Palisades Fire. For Phillips, the recognition remains deeply personal. She remembers being trapped with her dog and her final messages that were being sent to her husband. Dicks remembers telling his family about the rescue and wondering whether he would ever see Phillips again. The boulder remains a physical reminder of how a sudden obstacle became part of her escape from the flames.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Indians trust the classroom, see better opportunities abroad: Global survey
articles.summary: India News: A recent Ipsos survey highlights a paradox in Indian attitudes towards education and career prospects, showing optimism in local education while favoring opportunities abroad for youth.
articles.body: Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani. Not because the Ipsos Education Monitor survey mirrors the plot of the Shah Rukh Khan-Juhi Chawla film, but because the title neatly captures the contradiction in its India findings. Indians may believe better opportunities for growth and prosperity lie offshore, yet they remain remarkably bullish about their education system, their degrees and, above all, the future of their youth.More than half of Indian respondents rate the country’s education system as good. Three-fourths believe youth will have a better life than their parents. Nearly two-thirds think even young people from lesser privileged backgrounds have a bright future. And Indians remain strikingly convinced that a university degree still has value. However, ironically, 76% of Indian respondents say young people would have better opportunities by moving abroad.For some parameters, TOI looked at the subset of India’s position among the 16 individual G20 member countries included in the 31-country Ipsos survey. China, Russia and Saudi Arabia were not surveyed. The survey covered 23,537 online adults across the 31 countries between June and July 2026, with about 1,000 respondents in India. Ipsos in its methodology has cautioned that its India sample is more urban, educated and/or affluent than the general population and should be interpreted as reflecting the views of the country’s more “connected” segment.The 31-country average is an unweighted average of country results; it is not adjusted for the population size of each country.The robust belief in education, with a rider The first question was straightforward. How do people rate the overall quality of their country’s education system? In India, 51% called it good. Among the G20 countries covered by the survey, only Australia was higher, at 53%. The 31-country average was 33%. But that 51% is a number in retreat. India was at 65% in 2025, 69% in 2024 and 55% in 2023. The 14-point fall from 2025 is the steepest year-on-year decline among countries with comparable 2025 data.The contrast with several richer economies is sharp. Britain was at 43%, the US and Brazil at 32%, Italy at 29%, Japan at 24%, while France and Germany were both at 17%. That does not mean India has a better-performing education system than advanced economies. This is a matter of perception. And on that measure, Indians appear unusually confident. Just less than before.Optimism about Yuva ShaktiThe gap becomes even more striking when the question shifts from institutions to the people coming out of them. Asked whether young people in their country have a bright future, 72% of Indian respondents agreed. That was not merely the highest figure among the G20 countries covered. It was the highest among all 31 countries surveyed. The 31-country average was 45%.Within the surveyed G20 set, Australia and South Africa were next at 54%, followed by Mexico at 52% and Canada at 50%. France was at 22%. It is perhaps one of the strongest votes of confidence in the survey. Indians appear to have placed enormous hope in their youth to put the country on the right track and take it forward.The Indian dream remains intergenerationalOne of the hallmarks of an aspirational society like India is the belief in accumulating wealth and opportunity across generations. People believe that the hard work of one generation will make the lives of those that follow smoother. That belief gets backed in this survey. Three-fourths of Indian respondents, 75%, believe young people today will have a better life than their parents. The 31-country average is 48%.Indians are also optimistic about people escaping the poverty trap. 64% believe young people from poorer backgrounds have a bright future, compared with a 31-country average of 40%. India is the highest among the G20 countries covered on both measures. And 69% of Indian respondents believe the education system contributes to reducing social inequalities, again the highest among the surveyed G20 countries. That figure is also below earlier readings, 72% in 2024 and 79% in 2023.Together, these numbers suggest that Indian respondents continue to see education as a vehicle for upward social mobility. That belief becomes even clearer when the survey turns to higher education.In India, the college degree has not lost its promiseNITI Aayog’s recent Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047 report also points to the continuing pull of degree programmes, noting that vocational pathways are often not seen as credible, growth-oriented alternatives and that degrees can become the safer choice amid limited counselling, social bias and low trust in existing skill systems. The Ipsos survey, albeit with a more urban and connected Indian sample, points in a similar direction. 75% of Indian respondents say a college or university degree is very important to succeed in life. 78% believe it helps people go further in their careers. And 70% say degrees in their country offer good value for money.On the first measure, India is the highest among the G20 countries surveyed. On both the other measures, it ranks second. The contrast with several advanced economies is large. On whether a degree is good value for money, India’s 70% compares with 38% in the US, 41% in Germany, 30% in Japan and 28% in Britain. Ipsos itself finds a strong positive relationship across countries between believing that a degree helps a career and believing that it offers value for money.India trusts the curriculum, yet worries about the jobs connectionHere again, the Ipsos study broadly aligns with a concern flagged in NITI Aayog’s skilling report that education and credentials do not automatically translate into the skills and pathways that the labour market demands. The Ipsos survey shows a deep-seated faith in formal education and yet a growing realisation that job-market demands are at times different from what is being taught in the classroom.Asked whether the school curriculum adequately prepares students for future careers, 67% of Indians agree, the highest share among the G20 countries covered by the survey. Even here, the direction has been downward: 74% agreed in 2024, 72% in 2025 and 67% now.Yet in another question on the greatest challenges facing young people, 36% of Indian respondents select “education and training systems not matching labour market demands”. That too is the highest among the G20 countries in the survey.A bright future. Somewhere else?India again falls on one extreme of a scatter plot for its two seemingly contradictory sets of beliefs. On one hand, 72% say young people have a bright future. On the other hand, 76% say young people would have better opportunities by moving abroad. The 31-country average on that question is 62%.Indonesia and South Africa are even more likely to say opportunities are better overseas, at 87% and 80% respectively. Italy is at 79%. Romania matches India at 76%. But none combines that level of outward-looking aspiration with India’s exceptional optimism about the future of its young.This is perhaps the central finding of the entire report for India. Respondents may be optimistic about India’s young people precisely because they believe those young people possess education and skills that give them more options, including the option of leaving. The optimism may be about the people. The doubt may be about the location of opportunity.Social media? Restrict it. AI? Not necessarilyThe dichotomy in the approach of Indians extends to technology too. 78% support banning social media for children under 14, both inside and outside school. The 31-country average is 73%.Support has climbed 10 points in a year. India was at 68% in 2025 and 73% in 2024.On smartphones, 57% of Indian respondents favour a ban in schools, exactly matching the 31-country average. That is up from 50% last year and 52% in 2024. But attitudes to AI are different.Only 26% of Indian respondents say AI, including ChatGPT, should be banned in schools, compared with 39% across the 31 countries. Indian opinion on AI has moved sharply over the four editions of the survey. 39% wanted AI banned in schools in both 2025 and 2024, compared with just 16% in 2023. The 13-point drop from 2025 to 2026 is the largest year-on-year fall among countries with comparable 2025 data. Britain, the US and Poland moved in the other direction, rising to 52%, 56% and 46%, respectively.To sum up, India’s ‘connected’ population has not lost faith in education. Quite the opposite. It remains unusually convinced that education matters, degrees pay, children can surpass their parents and those from poorer homes can climb. What appears less certain is where that promise will ultimately be realised.Karmabhoomi and janmabhoomi may finally be different. That is the sobering realisation one can derive from this survey.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Million-dollar question: OpenAI claims to have an answer to 90-year old maths problem
articles.summary: US News: OpenAI says it has solved a 90-year-old mathematical problem in just 88 hours by using a new artificial intelligence model and around 10,000 AI agents.
articles.body: OpenAI says it has solved a 90-year-old mathematical problem in just 88 hours by using a new artificial intelligence model and around 10,000 AI agents. The problem, known as the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem, deals with how fluids move and is one of the major unsolved challenges in mathematics.According to a BBC report, the ChatGPT maker announced the result on Tuesday, calling it a "milestone" in the development of AI. However, the claim has not yet been independently verified and has not been accepted by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which offers a $1 million prize for solving the problem.AI agents worked around the clockOpenAI said it deployed about 10,000 AI agents to work on some of the world's most difficult mathematical questions after a new internal model showed strong mathematical abilities.The company began training the model in late August. It said the system was "significantly more capable" than its latest publicly released model.On September 1, OpenAI said it had heard rumours that two Millennium Prize problems had been solved. It then decided to put thousands of AI agents to work on some of the remaining problems.By September 5, roughly 88 hours after the agents began working, OpenAI said they had solved the Navier–Stokes problem.The scale of the effort was enormous. The AI agents exchanged nearly 3 million messages and generated about 130 billion output tokens while working on the problem.OpenAI estimates that running such a great effort would have cost around $10 million based on its own pricing for output from its most advanced models.Mathematician raises questions over timingOpenAI's announcement has also triggered controversy among mathematicians.Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematics professor at New York University, said he and Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at OpenAI rival Anthropic, had also been working on the Navier–Stokes problem.The pair had been using OpenAI's Codex tool as part of their work.Buckmaster said that on September 3, he learnt that information about their progress had been passed to OpenAI.He alleged that OpenAI began working on the Navier–Stokes problem only after information about their work had reached the company.Buckmaster included excerpts from emails exchanged with OpenAI and raised questions about the company's timing and methods.He said he had not yet read OpenAI's complete proof. But he felt compelled to make the information public.Buckmaster said he wanted to explain "what I was told, when, and what was proposed to me...because the alternative is to let a sequence of announcements say something I know to be false."OpenAI denies seeing their workOpenAI congratulated Buckmaster and Alpöge on their "concurrent work", describing it as "remarkable".The company said it had not seen any of their work through any means before they released it publicly.It also said that no user data was accessed during its work on the Navier–Stokes problem.However, OpenAI acknowledged one possibility that it said could not be ruled out completely."While unlikely, we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from their usage of our products helped improve our models⁠", the company said.OpenAI added that its proofs differ significantly from the work of Buckmaster and Alpöge."However, our proofs differ significantly, and even the precise results proved are different."Problem linked to turbulenceThe Navier–Stokes equations are used to describe the movement of fluids. They are central to the study of phenomena such as water flow and air movement.But despite being studied for around 90 years, important aspects of the equations have remained unproven.The problem is also closely linked to turbulence, a phenomenon that scientists still do not fully understand.The Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem is one of the mathematical challenges selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute for its Millennium Prize.OpenAI is not claiming the $1 million prizeDespite calling the result a major milestone, OpenAI is not claiming the Millennium Prize.The company said its solution resolved two of the four statements required in the proof set out by the Millennium Prize."Our goal in releasing this result is to report on the substantial progress of our AI models", OpenAI said on Tuesday. "We do not intend to claim the Millennium Prize for this result."The solution will need to undergo independent scrutiny before its significance can be fully established.The Clay Mathematics Institute has not publicly accepted OpenAI's result as a solution to the Millennium Prize problem.What the result could mean for AIThe claim is significant because it suggests that AI systems may be moving beyond solving routine mathematical problems and beginning to tackle questions that have challenged mathematicians for generations.OpenAI's experiment also highlights the growing use of multiple AI agents working together on complex tasks.But the result still faces an important test: independent mathematicians will need to examine the proof and determine whether it stands up to rigorous scrutiny.For now, OpenAI is presenting the work as evidence of rapid progress in AI rather than as a completed solution to one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A Napa art center is giving up development rights on 162 of its 217 acres; the deal protects 75% of the estate while directing up to $1.85 million back to the arts
articles.summary: US News: A major conservation agreement in California’s Napa Valley is set to permanently protect much of the sprawling landscape surrounding the di Rosa Cente.
articles.body: A major conservation agreement in California’s Napa Valley is set to permanently protect much of the sprawling landscape surrounding the di Rosa Center for Contemporary Art, while potentially providing the institution with up to $1.85 million to support its cultural operations. Announced August 25 by the Land Trust of Napa County, the deal brings together the di Rosa Center and the Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District in an effort to preserve both the land and the arts center’s long-standing connection to it.The agreement covers 162 acres of di Rosa’s 217-acre property in the Carneros region, placing roughly three-quarters of the estate beyond future private development. The protected area includes Milliken Peak, a 732-foot summit with sweeping views across Carneros, as well as watershed areas, wildlife habitat, and the hillsides surrounding the center’s cultural campus.The move is particularly significant for di Rosa, whose identity has always been rooted in the relationship between art and nature. The center describes its property as a 217-acre destination featuring galleries, a lake, walking trails and outdoor sculptures. Under the new arrangement, the surrounding landscape will be preserved as public open space, reinforcing the very setting that has helped define di Rosa for decades.What happens to the remaining landThe deal does not mean di Rosa is giving up its entire Napa operation. The center will retain ownership and programming on roughly 53.5 acres that make up its principal cultural campus. That area includes the galleries and other facilities that support its exhibitions and public programs.The Land Trust of Napa County will hold the permanent conservation easement over the 162 acres, while the Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District is expected to own and operate the future public parkland. The financial arrangement is also designed to help di Rosa remain viable. An initial $500,000 allocation is secured for the arts center, while another $1.35 million would be available if voters approve Measure B in November. Together, that could bring the support connected to the deal to $1.85 million.A future trail to Milliken PeakOne of the most intriguing parts of the plan is what could eventually happen on the protected hillsides. Plans envision a roughly two-mile trail leading to the summit of Milliken Peak. If completed, it would create a new public hiking destination while opening up views that are currently inaccessible to most visitors.The landscape would also remain closely tied to the art center’s identity. di Rosa has historically incorporated large-scale sculptures into its grounds, including works in its Sculpture Meadow leading toward Milliken Peak. Its existing programming includes guided hikes that combine the property’s art and natural surroundings. The future trail could take that concept further, with plans to place additional large sculptures from the di Rosa collection along the route.For now, however, the ridge remains temporarily closed while planning for the future park continues. di Rosa is expected to continue offering its regular hiking programs in the meantime.Preserving more than a viewThe significance of the agreement extends beyond keeping an attractive Napa ridgeline undeveloped. The Land Trust describes the property as part of an ecological corridor, with the conservation easement helping protect habitat and local watersheds. The arrangement also fits into a much longer history of conservation around di Rosa: the center says its property has been protected through Napa County land-trust conservation measures while continuing to function as an art destination.For Napa, the result could be an unusual combination: land that becomes increasingly accessible to the public without losing the artistic character that made the property distinctive in the first place. If Measure B receives voter approval in November, the proposed funding would also give di Rosa additional resources to maintain its cultural mission while the surrounding hillsides move toward their future as public open space. In a region where land, development, conservation and culture frequently compete for space, the di Rosa agreement attempts to make all four coexist on the same 217 acres.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: Tech News News: Canadian aerospace company Bombardier has highlighted its growing presence in America. This follows US President Donald Trump's call for the company t.
articles.body: Canadian aerospace company Bombardier has highlighted its growing presence in America. This follows US President Donald Trump's call for the company to build its aircraft in the country if it wants access to the American market. Trump made the remarks as Canada introduced retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion worth of US goods, adding to tensions between the two countries.​“Bombardier values its great partnership with American companies and its US employees. Our plan is to continue to invest in our people, our customers and the communities in which we operate across the country,” the company said in a statement.​Bombardier said it already has a significant presence across the U.S., with direct employment in more than 20 states and facilities in 10 states. The company also pointed to its American supply chain and plans to expand its defence and service operations in the country.​The company’s response came after, in a recent post shared on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! If they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a ‘piggybank.’”​Where Bombardier operates in the US​Bombardier said its American workers are based across the country, with sites in Kansas, Texas, Arizona, Florida, Connecticut, Illinois, Delaware, California, Washington DC and New Jersey. The company has direct employment presence in more than 20 states.​The company also said its aircraft support tens of thousands of U.S. jobs through its American operations and supply chain. Bombardier works with approximately 2,800 American companies across 47 states and spends more than $2.5 billion with suppliers each year.​Its U.S. aerospace presence dates back to the business jet industry, including the legacy of Learjet in Wichita, Kansas, where the first business jets entered service.​Bombardier aircraft use American-made components​Bombardier also pointed to American-made components used in its aircraft, including engines, avionics and other key systems supplied by US companies.​The company said American workers produce the wings for its fastest business jet at its facility in Red Oak, Texas. Bombardier also makes flight control components at its facility in the Los Angeles, California, area.​Bombardier has announced plans to expand its defence activities and service network in the US. It also plans to inaugurate a new facility in Fort Wayne, Indiana, later this year.​Why Donald Trump targeted Bombardier​Trump's comments came hours after Canada implemented retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion worth of U.S. imports. The duties were introduced in response to tariffs the Trump administration imposed on Canadian goods.​Trump also called for Canada-origin products to be excluded from a US government programme that purchases commercial products. In a separate Truth Social post, he accused Ottawa of “ripping us off for years” and claimed that US companies are barred from equivalent Canadian programmes.​“From now on, NO RECIPROCITY – NO ACCESS!” Trump wrote. His latest comments revived an earlier dispute over Bombardier's access to the U.S. market.​Bombardier has faced US tariff threats before​The first Trump administration imposed a nearly 300% tariff on new Bombardier passenger jets following a complaint from Boeing. A US trade panel later rejected the tariff in 2018.​Bombardier subsequently sold its commercial C-Series aircraft programme to Airbus, which now produces the aircraft in Alabama under the A220 name. The company also ended production of its Canadair Regional Jet, or CRJ, series in 2020 after selling the programme to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.​Trump had also threatened earlier this year to decertify Bombardier aircraft in the US and impose tariffs, after accusing Canada of blocking American aircraft manufacturer Gulfstream from doing business in the country.​Canada's Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon disputed that claim at the time.​“Gulfstream aircraft is and can be freely sold and operated in Canada,” MacKinnon said in a statement to The Washington Post.​Neither the threatened aircraft decertification nor the tariffs ultimately materialised, and Canada subsequently certified several Gulfstream models.​Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Watch: Trump shares edited clip of King Charles walking away from fainting worker
articles.summary: US News: Donald Trump called King Charles “the greatest king, in my book” during the monarch’s US state visit in April. Months later, the tone had shifted shar.
articles.body: Donald Trump called King Charles “the greatest king, in my book” during the monarch’s US state visit in April. Months later, the tone had shifted sharply: on Labor Day, Trump included Charles in a three-minute Truth Social montage portraying several public figures unfavourably, using an edited 2020 clip that omitted footage showing the King staying near a worker who had collapsed.The montage contrasts clips involving the other figures with footage of Trump. Captions include "the people's president" and "the side of Trump the media doesn't show you", while Christina Perri's A Thousand Years plays throughout.One scene shows Trump picking up a US Marine's cap, while another shows him giving a salute at a repatriation ceremony, while other footage features him embracing veterans, greeting law-enforcement officers and comforting relatives of fallen service members.Edited Charles clip omits aftermathThe Charles footage comes from a July 2020 visit to an Asda distribution centre in Bristol. Charles, who was Prince of Wales at the time, was speaking to an employee when the man suddenly collapsed. Trump's montage shows his initial reaction and then cuts to him moving away.According to the BBC, the full recording shared on YouTube by The Royal Family Channel continues beyond that point. Charles reaches towards the employee as he starts to fall and remains nearby while others attend to him in the full video. Contemporary reports said he continued with the visit after being told the worker appeared to be coming round. The employee recovered quickly and later resumed his conversation with Charles. Neither that later interaction nor the period in which Charles stayed close while the man was assisted appears in Trump's version.Montage also features Macron, Biden and ObamaFormer US president Barack Obama is shown stepping away from Marine One with a paper cup in one hand and raising the other in salute towards US Marines, while former US president Joe Biden appears in footage from a military repatriation ceremony, where the clip captures him briefly looking down towards his wrist.French President Emmanuel Macron is shown at the Elysee Palace as a ceremonial guardsman behind him appears to lose balance and fall, while Macron remains in the foreground.The post does not explain why Charles, Macron, Biden and Obama were selected for the comparison or why Trump shared the montage now. With no White House response to questions about the video, the reason for its timing and choice of figures remains unclear.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: AI agents may soon be able to make UPI payments for users: How it may work, what will be allowed and what not
articles.summary: Tech News News: ​NPCI may soon allow AI agents to make UPI payments on your behalf. A Reuters report citing three people familiar with the matter claims India is prep.
articles.body: ​NPCI may soon allow AI agents to make UPI payments on your behalf. A Reuters report citing three people familiar with the matter claims India is preparing a framework that would let artificial intelligence agents make small digital payments on UPI without approval for every transaction. The move could make UPI one of the world's largest networks built for agentic payments, and place India among the first countries with national infrastructure of this kind.​UPI is already the world's largest retail fast-payment system by transaction volume, according to a 2025 IMF. Data from NPCI suggest the network processed 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August, its highest monthly volume yet. Google Pay and PhonePe together account for roughly three-fourths of that volume.​What is Unified Agent ProtocolThe proposed Unified Agent Protocol (UAP) would create a common, interoperable system for registering, verifying and authorising AI agents that transact through UPI. The Reuters report claimed the protocol was expected to be unveiled at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai; however, NPCI has yet to confirm its announcement.​UPI was built around a human user approving each payment. Under the agentic model, a user would instead grant an AI agent defined authority such as a spending cap or restrictions on transaction type rather than confirming every purchase, according to the Economic Times.​How it may work and what will be allowedAccording to Reuters sources, the protocol is expected to draw on two existing UPI mechanisms: UPI Circle, which lets a primary account holder delegate payment authority to a secondary user, and Reserve Pay, which lets customers block funds for multiple debits. Banks currently cap such blocks at Rs 10,000 for up to 90 days, though sources told Reuters this limit may be revisited for agentic use.​Low-value, frequent purchases such as groceries are likely to be among the first use cases, with e-commerce platforms well placed to capture early demand, one source told Reuters. NPCI reportedly expects use cases to grow more sophisticated over time, with agents eventually placing orders around sale offers or making investments based on price thresholds.​Spending limits, audit trails and identity checks are expected to be built into the system, so that transactions can be verified as authorised and agents confirmed as legitimate. NPCI also reportedly plans to build in a liability framework, though details were not disclosed in the report​Industry is already movingSome groundwork exists outside NPCI's framework. Pine Labs has launched its own protocol, P3P, letting AI agents complete UPI payments after a single upfront authorisation. "The consumer authorises once, upfront. After that, the agent browses, selects, negotiates, and pays. No human authentication. No interruption. No friction," the company said. Gullak's gold-savings AI agent already uses P3P.​Mastercard completed its first authenticated agentic transaction in New Delhi in June, the report added, while Visa is separately building similar capabilities in India. Meanwhile, Razorpay has also launched an Agent Studio for merchants in March using Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.​Agentic AI is listed as one of three core technology pillars at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, where discussions are expected to focus on establishing an agent's identity, defining its authority and maintaining audit trails as such payments enter India's financial infrastructure.​Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Georgia O'Keeffe bought a small Ghost Ranch home in 1940 and spent decades painting the surrounding desert; a conservation plan is now protecting 6,000 acres from development
articles.summary: US News: Long before the desert landscapes of Northern New Mexico became icons of American art, they were simply a vast meeting of red cliffs, golden mesas, op.
articles.body: Long before the desert landscapes of Northern New Mexico became icons of American art, they were simply a vast meeting of red cliffs, golden mesas, open skies and rugged wilderness. For artist Georgia O’Keeffe, that landscape became both a home and a source of inspiration. Now, decades after she first made Ghost Ranch part of her life, a new conservation effort is working to ensure the scenery that shaped her art remains largely unchanged for generations to come. The National Ghost Ranch Foundation and the Presbyterian Foundation announced a partnership with the State of New Mexico and the New Mexico Land Conservancy in 2025 to protect approximately 6,000 acres surrounding Ghost Ranch. According to a report by Presbyterian Foundation, under the Ghost Ranch Conservation Plan, the land, water and wildlife habitat are being protected through conservation easements. These voluntary agreements safeguard land for conservation purposes while allowing its owners to retain ownership, the report states. The goal has been not only to protect the area's natural beauty but also to ensure Ghost Ranch can continue operating its educational and retreat programs sustainably for years to come.A legacy supported by public fundingThe first phase of the conservation effort received $930,000 from New Mexico's Natural Heritage Conservation Act Program through the Energy, Minerals & Natural Resources Department. The funding came from the Land of Enchantment Legacy Fund, a state initiative supporting land and water conservation, agriculture and outdoor recreation. According to the report, the money helped cover transaction costs associated with establishing the conservation easements. The New Mexico Land Conservancy helped held the easements in trust for public benefit and traditional land users, working with the Presbyterian Foundation, the National Ghost Ranch Foundation and the State of New Mexico.Preserving the Ghost Ranch experienceAccording to the same report, the conservation plan is designed to protect the surrounding landscape without changing the core visitor experience. The easements is said to not cover the 550 acres containing Ghost Ranch's main facilities, including its visitor center, trails, lodging, stables and museums. That distinction means the thousands of people who visit Ghost Ranch each year can continue to explore and experience the site while the larger surrounding landscape receives long-term protection from development. New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham has called the initiative an opportunity to preserve the vistas that attracted O’Keeffe to the region and continue to define Northern New Mexico's distinctive character.The landscape behind O’Keeffe’s ArtFor the unversed, Ghost Ranch sits amid the dramatic red and yellow cliffs of the Piedra Lumbre, about 65 miles northwest of Santa Fe along U.S. 84. The region became closely associated with O’Keeffe, whose paintings transformed its cliffs, mesas, bones and expansive skies into some of the most recognizable images in American art.O’Keeffe bought a small house and seven acres at Ghost Ranch in 1940 and also maintained a larger home and studio in nearby Abiquiú. Those properties are now separately owned and managed by the Georgia O’Keeffe Museum in Santa Fe. While the new conservation plan does not directly protect those properties, it preserves many of the landscapes that inspired her work, including views toward Abiquiú Lake, the Rio Chama and Cerro Pedernal, known in Tewa as Tsip’in.A vision that continuesGhost Ranch's conservation story stretches back generations. Arthur and Phoebe Pack donated the land in 1955 to the Board of Christian Education, now part of the Presbyterian Foundation. Their vision was to preserve Ghost Ranch as an educational and retreat center while protecting its surrounding lands. The new conservation plan carries that vision forward. By bringing government agencies, nonprofit organizations and landowners together, the partnership aims to ensure that the landscape O’Keeffe found so compelling remains a place of nature, culture, learning and inspiration, rather than becoming another developed piece of the American West.Images Courtesy: Wikipedia and Presbyterian FoundationCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: US strike sinks Iranian tanker, sparking retaliatory missile barrage at Jordan
articles.summary: The US military struck five Iranian tankers on Tuesday, sinking one, after Iran fired ballistic missiles at a US Navy warship, in a fresh escalation of fight...
articles.body:
The US military struck five Iranian tankers on Tuesday, sinking one, after Iran fired ballistic missiles at a US Navy warship, in a fresh escalation of fighting in the Middle East.

The attacks prompted a significant retaliation from Iran, which launched a missile barrage toward regional US ally Jordan, saying it was targeting US military assets.

Four crude oil carriers in the Gulf of Oman and one near Kharg Island –– a hub for Iranian oil exports in the Persian Gulf –– were struck on Tuesday, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said.

One of the ships, identified as the M/T Riesco, is seen on fire and sinking in the Gulf of Oman in a video posted to X by the military.

US forces instructed the crews of the vessels they targeted to abandon ship prior to striking, CENTCOM said. Iranian state media said the crew of two vessels have been taken ashore in lifeboats.

The US strikes were in response to two Iranian attempts to attack a US Navy ship over the past two days. The US ship evaded the missiles and was continuing to patrol regional waters, CENTCOM said, adding that "no American personnel were harmed."

The exchange of strikes comes as the US has focused its strategy on ramping up economic pressure on the Tehran regime, by prioritizing striking or disabling targets around the Strait of Hormuz, conducting escort operations for commercial vessels through the key waterway and maintaining its naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran retaliated to the US strikes by launching missiles at Jordan, saying it was targeting Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, a key facility used by US forces.

The Jordanian army said its air defenses dealt with 20 ballistic missiles, 18 of them successfully destroyed, with two falling in unpopulated areas. No deaths were reported, the army said.

The latest strikes come after US forces hit three Iranian crude oil carriers over the weekend, in response to an Iranian attempt to attack a US aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer.

The attack on Jordan "represents a significant geographic expansion of direct Iranian military activity and demonstrates the growing risk of the conflict spilling beyond the principal belligerents," shipping intelligence and tracking firm Marisks said in an update on Wednesday.

Iran's repeated attempts to attack US warships and the increased "quality and quantity" of the missiles it fired at US targets in the region showed "a pattern of gradual escalation," said Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group think tank, on X .

Iran also threatened on Tuesday to target oil tankers near Bahraini and Kuwaiti ports.

"We warn all crews aboard oil tankers in the vicinity of ports in Kuwait and Bahrain — which host these (American) terrorists and are partners in their hostile actions — to immediately leave their vessels, whether they are at anchor or docked at the ports, as the vessels will be targeted," state broadcaster IRIB quoted the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as saying.

Azizi said an Iranian attack on tankers stationed in ports in the region, rather than those attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, would be a first.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, during his trip to Colombia , warned Tehran that the US would respond every time Iran targeted its naval ships.

"Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships and for every time they do that, or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers," he told reporters in the city of Barranquilla.

As part of the US' pressure campaign on Tehran, the Trump administration also took sweeping actions against Iran's airline industry on Tuesday. The sanctions affect 27 Iranian airlines and nine service providers and sales agents accused of providing services to Mahan Air, which has been sanctioned since 2011. The private airline is accused of providing key support to the IRGC.

The US campaign has put Iran under unprecedented pressure , forcing its fatigued population to endure still more strain. But its leaders are quick to downplay the impact of sanctions.

"After Washington failed to achieve its objectives through either sanctions or war, its 'innovative' solution is: more sanctions!! Are you serious?!!" Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X on Tuesday.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN's Eleni Giokos, Eyad Kourdi, Thomas Bordeaux and Yasha Saebi contributed reporting.

articles.title: “Muse, help me quit Instagram”: Mark Zuckerberg introduces Meta’s New AI agent, the internet’s hilarious reactions took a very different turn
articles.summary: Trending News: Mark Zuckerberg has introduced Muse on Instagram with a simple promise: a personal AI agent designed to do more than just answer questions, it can hel.
articles.body: Mark Zuckerberg has introduced Muse on Instagram with a simple promise: a personal AI agent designed to do more than just answer questions, it can help users actually get things done.“Meet @Muse, the personal agent that helps you get things done,” he captioned the video on Instagram.A little after that polished introduction, the comment section took the announcement in a very different direction.One of the funniest reactions to Mark Zuckerberg’s latest AI pitch came from a user who apparently had no interest in adding another AI assistant to their life. Their request was brutally simple: “Muse, help me quit instagram.”And that was only the beginning. Beneath Zuckerberg’s post introducing Muse as a “personal agent that helps you get things done,” commenters asked whether it could replace Meta employees, complained that it was unavailable in their countries, and questioned what would happen to their private data.The reactions reveal something interesting about the moment Meta is entering: people are fascinated by AI agents, but many are still trying to decide whether they want an AI that can actually act on their behalf.“Muse, help me quit Instagram”The joke lands because Muse is a Meta product being introduced by the same company that owns Instagram. Instead of asking the new AI to book a holiday, send an email or organise a schedule, the commenter essentially asked it to help escape one of Meta’s biggest platforms.Another commenter took the joke in an even more existential direction:“Can Muse erase Meta out of my life?” @philgreissThat was followed by a much more blunt response: “😂 privacy? Yeah, sure” @ddkarjalaThe privacy jokes were not entirely random. Muse is designed to connect with apps containing highly personal information, including email, calendars, payments, shopping, health and smart-home systems. Meta says users choose which apps Muse can access and can revoke those permissions.Among the jokes, one comment stood out for being unusually specific:“Does it replace meta employees? 🤔” @josesiles.dataThat question has an unusually timely edge. Meta has spent much of 2026 experimenting with AI agents and AI-driven changes to its workforce, although an ambitious internal effort to dramatically reduce staffing through AI was later scaled back after problems with performance, reliability and employee resistance.Not everyone was jokingSome commenters were genuinely excited.“Can’t wait to try 👏” @technologyAnother wrote: “I’ll immediately install muse😍”Others were simply frustrated that they could not access it yet:“I don’t see it in the Mexico AppStore yet 😢” @luisitocomunicaAnd: “Only available in US? Cuz I can’t see it on my App Store” @itskaiwanMeta describes Muse as an agent that can work across multiple services and continue carrying out tasks in the background. That is a significant step beyond simply answering a question in a chat window.So while Zuckerberg’s post presented Muse as a personal assistant, the comment section was busy asking a different question: can an AI agent be trusted with your life when it can actually do things, rather than merely tell you how to do them?Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Hurricane Lowell leaves at least one dead, knocks out power in Kauai County
articles.summary: US News: At least one person died on Oahu after Hurricane Lowell swept past Hawaii, while wind gusts above 80mph knocked out power to around 90% of homes and b.
articles.body: At least one person died on Oahu after Hurricane Lowell swept past Hawaii, while wind gusts above 80mph knocked out power to around 90% of homes and businesses in Kauai County as the state began cleaning up Tuesday, according to PowerOutage.com.The death occurred after a tree fell on a tent occupied by a homeless man, Hawaii governor Josh Green said. Kauai County officials also reported storm-related injuries but did not say how many people were hurt or describe their injuries.The county's power provider had not given an estimated restoration time and warned that some outages could be prolonged.Green said Lowell had likely caused damage worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Homes and other structures in Kauai County were damaged by wind and storm surge.Flights cancelled as shelters house more than 300All flights at Lihue Airport, Kauai's primary airport, were cancelled Monday afternoon. Hawaii's Department of Transportation said the airport would reopen when it was safe to do so. More than 300 people and dozens of pets were in Kauai County emergency shelters Tuesday morning.State and county offices and public schools were closed Tuesday in Kauai County and on Oahu. Kauai Community College was also closed as cleanup and damage assessments continued.More than 300 National Guard members were deployed across Hawaii. Transportation crews were helping deal with mudslides and storm damage to roads, while other crews were working to restore electricity at hospitals. “There are currently downed power lines, downed trees, debris all over Kauai, so we are really urging folks to stay in place,” Alan Clinton, situation unit leader with Kauai County, said.650 Kauai residences under voluntary evacuation advisoriesAbout 650 residences on Kauai's south and west shores were placed under voluntary evacuation advisories because of the storm-surge threat. Dozens of guests at a hotel in Kapa'a were moved to shelters Monday. Green said waves driven ashore by Lowell “damaged a lot of the area right around the shoreline”.The effects extended beyond Kauai. More than 30,000 customers lost power on Oahu during the storm as tropical-storm-force wind gusts hit the island. High surf also reached a handful of ground-floor units at a condominium in western Oahu.In Maui, coastal flooding closed roads in South Maui and parts of Maui Nui. Maui County reported debris on roads, damage to transport infrastructure and park and service closures.Lowell passes less than 50 miles from NiihauLowell's centre passed less than 50 miles from Niihau in Kauai County while the hurricane was a Category 2 system. It was the strongest hurricane to affect Hawaii's main islands since Category 4 Hurricane Iniki in 1992.It was forecast to weaken to a tropical storm as it moved farther north from Hawaii. Its strongest winds had already subsided, although forecasters expected more rainfall across areas soaked by the storm.More than a foot of rain had fallen at higher elevations on Kauai. Oahu's Koolau mountains received between 5 and 9 inches, while most other areas recorded between 1 and 3 inches.Forecasters expected surf conditions to improve as Tuesday progressed. A high surf warning remained in effect through Tuesday afternoon for south-facing shores of Kauai County, Oahu County, Maui County and the Big Island.Five storms already match typical Central Pacific seasonThe National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has forecast as many as 13 named storms in the Central Pacific this season, compared with about five in a typical year.Five named storms, including Lowell, have already formed in or moved into the region. Two other tropical systems had threatened Hawaii over the previous three weeks.El Nino is contributing to the increased storm potential. Warmer waters in the Central Pacific and weaker upper-level winds create more favourable conditions for tropical systems, while ocean temperatures are also rising over the longer term because of climate change.With Lowell moving farther north, crews were restoring power, dealing with damaged roads and assessing the storm's impact across the affected islands. “We’re doing what we can to recover, but this was a very serious storm,” Green said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Information sharing is through intelligence channels': Israel denies report UAE leader warned Netanyahu days before Oct 7 attack
articles.summary: Middle East News: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office has rejected reports that he was warned in advance about the October 2023, Hamas attacks by UAE Pre.
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office has rejected reports that he was warned in advance about the October 2023, Hamas attacks by UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed.In a post on X, the Israeli Prime Minister’s Office said any exchange of relevant information took place only through intelligence channels between the two countries.“The press reports are false. No warning was given to the Prime Minister by the United Arab Emirates before October 7. If there was any relevant information, it was passed through intelligence channels between the two countries,” it posted.According to a new investigative report published by Israeli newspaper Haaretz, Mohammed bin Zayed had warned Netanyahu that Hamas’ then-leader Yahya Sinwar was preparing a “major attack” on Israel.Netanyahu, however, did not share the warning with Israel’s senior security leadership.Around 10 days after their reported conversation, Hamas launched its attack on Israel on October 7, 2023.The Haaretz report is based on the new book "Kidnapped: 843 Days of Abandonment." It claimed that Mohammed bin Zayed spoke to Netanyahu for 45 minutes from Abu Dhabi.Bin Zayed also reportedly urged Netanyahu to address broader sources of instability, including Gaza’s economic situation and rising tensions in the West Bank.According to a UAE presidential advisor interviewed for the book, bin Zayed was “surprised” by Netanyahu’s response, as the Israeli prime minister did not appear “alarmed”.“He (Netanyahu) said that he believed Hamas was preparing to act in the West Bank and assured him that Israel was ready to respond to any scenario,” the report quoted the adviser as saying.The Emirati leader later discussed the warning with then-CIA Director William J Burns. Bin Zayed reportedly expressed concern that “something there is about to explode” and said Netanyahu had instead focused on the West Bank.Notwithstanding the clarification, the report is likely to pile further pressure on Netanyahu, who has repeatedly been accused of ignoring warning signs in the days leading up to the Hamas attack.The claims are also significant as they come ahead of the Israeli Knesset elections, scheduled for October 27, with Netanyahu seeking a seventh term in office.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Attack on one is attack on all': Pakistan warns Houthis, invokes Mecca defence pact
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan warned Tuesday that its newly formed defence alliance with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye could be activated if the conflict in Yemen spills into S.
articles.body: Pakistan warned Tuesday that its newly formed defence alliance with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye could be activated if the conflict in Yemen spills into Saudi territory, saying there should be “no ambiguity” that an attack on any one of the three members would be treated as an attack on all.Pakistan’s defence minister Khawaja Asif said the agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in Makkah last month was defensive in nature and required the three countries to respond if any member came under unprovoked aggression.“There should be no ambiguity; there is no need for any clarity that this is a joint defence agreement,” Asif said in an interview with Geo TV. He added that Pakistan was “bound by the terms and conditions of this pact” and would honour its commitments to Saudi Arabia if required.His comments came hours after Iran-aligned Houthi forces launched a wave of missile and drone attacks on southern Saudi Arabia, targeting cities as well as economic and energy infrastructure. At least 73 civilians were injured, according to the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen.Asif stressed that the alliance did not give its members a mandate to launch offensive operations against another country on their own initiative.“This is not an aggressive agreement under which the three countries would, on their own initiative, attack another country. But if there is any aggression against one member state, all three member states will respond,” he said.The minister said he was not aware of any contact between Islamabad and Riyadh following the latest Houthi attacks. He also expressed hope that tensions would ease, while warning the Houthis against extending the Yemen conflict into Saudi Arabia.“If they try to export them, the clauses of this agreement to counter aggression will become operative,” Asif said.Pakistan prime minister Shehbaz Sharif separately condemned the Houthi attacks, describing them as “cowardly” and saying they threatened civilian lives as well as regional peace and security. He said Pakistan stood in “unwavering” solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed support for the kingdom's sovereignty, security and territorial integrity.The Saudi-led coalition said the attacks had temporarily disrupted operations at some targeted sites, while specialised teams worked to contain fires and secure the facilities. Riyadh also warned against continued attacks on civilians and commercial shipping.The Houthis said the attacks were retaliation for recent Saudi airstrikes on areas of northwestern Yemen under their control. The group had also accused Saudi Arabia of bombing a prison in Al Hazm on Monday, killing at least 11 people.Asif described the Houthis as “non-state actors” and said sympathy for Iran's position in its ongoing conflict with the United States existed across parts of the Muslim world, including Yemen. But he cautioned against allowing those sentiments to widen the conflict.He also said the Mecca alliance could act as a deterrent without necessarily requiring a military response to every attack.“We don't need to respond to a brick with a stone,” Asif said, arguing that the combined military capabilities of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye should themselves serve as a deterrent.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Pilot and four medical workers killed in air ambulance helicopter crash amid Borneo wildfires
articles.summary: Helicopter crashes in Sarawak, Malaysia, as haze from Indonesian wildfires hampers search
articles.body:
Five people, including a pilot and four health ministry staff, died in a helicopter crash near Long Lellang airport in Sarawak, Malaysia.

The helicopter, a Bo-105, crashed after the Flight Information Service notified the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia of the incident at 3.58pm the previous day.

Search and recovery operations were hindered by hazy conditions caused by forest fires in Indonesia, with rescuers unable to use air services and the crash site requiring a ten-hour journey by road.

Five people died when a "flying doctor" service helicopter crashed in Malaysia on Tuesday, authorities said, as haze from Indonesian wildfires complicated search efforts.

Health minister, Dzulkefly Ahmad, said in a statement that initial information showed a pilot and four health ministry staff were aboard the helicopter when it crashed near Long Lellang short take-off and landing airport in Sarawak, on the island of Borneo.

Those on board included a medical officer, an assistant medical officer, and two nurses who were on official duty, he said.

A disaster management committee official in Miri, Sarawak, confirmed to the state news agency Bernama that all five people aboard had died in the crash.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said the helicopter, a Bo-105, was carrying five people when it crashed after the Flight Information Service notified the authority of the incident at 3.58pm the previous day.

Investigators from the Air Accident Investigation Bureau are expected to arrive in Miri at 2pm on Wednesday to begin examining the crash, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia's chief executive, Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud, quoted by the New Straits Times .

"The helicopter wreckage at the crash site will remain undisturbed following instructions from the AAIB," he said. "The site has been cordoned off and secured."

Search and recovery operations were set to resume on Wednesday, with a Fire and Rescue Department helicopter carrying 18 personnel departing Miri for Long Lellang at 7am.

Two police helicopters carrying 11 personnel were due to join the operation, along with four police officers from Long Lama and four Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency personnel from Miri. Police are expected to oversee the identification of victims at Miri Hospital, including DNA comparisons with their families.

Malaysia's "flying doctor" service typically uses aircraft to provide medical care, emergency transport, and clinical services to rural or isolated regions.

Search operations on Tuesday were hampered by hazy conditions, with rescuers barred from using air services, Sarawak police commissioner Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said in a statement. He added that the crash site was in a remote area requiring a ten-hour journey by road.

Sarawak has been badly affected by haze from forest fires in neighbouring Indonesia, with many areas recording unhealthy air quality levels, according to government data released on Wednesday. Malaysia declared an emergency last week in Sarawak's Serian district after air pollution reached hazardous levels, though the declaration was lifted after air quality improved.

articles.title: Hong Kong's first post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa dies at age 89
articles.summary: Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's first leader after the former British colony was handed back to China, has died aged 89, his office said on Wednesday. Tung died p...
articles.body:
Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's first leader after the handover from Britain to China in 1997, has passed away at the age of 89.

Tung, a businessman and shipping magnate, was selected for the post by a Beijing-backed committee despite being considered politically inexperienced.

During his tenure, Hong Kong faced challenges such as a financial crisis, the SARS outbreak, and widespread protests against proposed legislation, leading to Tung's resignation in 2005.

Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's first leader after the former British colony was handed back to China, has died aged 89, his office said on Wednesday.

Tung died peacefully surrounded by his family on Tuesday, his office said. Hong Kong's acting chief executive John Lee said Tung's contributions to the city had been "exceptionally significant."

Tung became Hong Kong's first chief executive after Britain handed the territory back to China in 1997. Under the "one country, two systems" framework, Beijing promised Hong Kong certain freedoms.

"I firmly believe, as a Special Administrative Region of China, the future of Hong Kong will be more glorious and more successful," Tung said in his inaugural speech on July 1, 1997.

Born in Shanghai, Tung was a businessman and shipping magnate who was selected for the post by a Beijing-backed committee. He was considered politically inexperienced.

At the start of his tenure, a severe financial and currency crisis that originated in Thailand spread across Asia, hitting Hong Kong among other things through the bursting of a property bubble.

Despite criticism of the government's response, Tung was re-elected in 2002 for a second five-year term.

In 2003, the infectious disease SARS hit the financial hub, killing more than 280 people. That summer, hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets to protest against a planned anti-subversion law, which critics said could threaten Hong Kong's freedoms.

The government later withdrew the proposed legislation.

Calls for greater political participation and direct elections for Hong Kong's government grew among parts of the population. Tung followed Beijing's line and rejected the demands.

He stepped down early in 2005, citing his health.

articles.title: Bharat Ratna scientist prof CNR Rao, 92, gets SIR notice over name mismatch
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Eminent scientist and Bharat Ratna awardee Prof C N R Rao, 92, has been summoned for a hearing to establish his identity after his name was.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Eminent scientist and Bharat Ratna awardee Prof C N R Rao, 92, has been summoned for a hearing to establish his identity after his name was flagged during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka.Rao has been issued a notice citing a self-name mismatch. The 2002 electoral roll records him as “Prof C N R Rao”, while the current roll carries an additional “f”, listing him as “Proff C N R Rao”.A self-name mismatch occurs when the details provided by an elector in the SIR enumeration form, based on the 2002 roll, do not match the corresponding entry in the current electoral roll.Under the procedure, only the person named in the notice can attend the hearing. Rao has consequently been asked to appear in person at a venue in Malleshwaram near the Indian Institute of Science (IISc).Rao was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2014 and is the third scientist to receive the country’s highest civilian honour.Economist Amartya Sen was also flagged for a similar spelling discrepancy.
